text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - elevated error rates from multi-GPU serving pool (prod-serving-3). auto-pager fired for collective failures. root_ts=3659997777

sara: seeing a flurry of container restarts on nodes gnode-07/08/09. app logs show repeated CUDA Xid 73 / device-side assert and NCCL timeouts. customer-facing errors spiking ~3.2% -> 9% in last 2m. rolling errors across tensor/pipeline parallel replicas.

jonah: adding @eng-sre-oncall. can you confirm severity? this is impacting 2 paying customers running large batching pipelines.

eng-sre-oncall: I'm on it. severity=P1 due to customer impact + autoscale churn. starting triage. please post logs and any stack dumps here.

maria: logs attached (excerpt below) — repeated patterns: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] NCCL WARN Call to AllReduce timed out after 30000ms
[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] NCCL ERROR ncclCommAbort on rank 3
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] driver: Xid 73: GPU has fallen off the bus
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] containerd: process crashed (exit 137) on /srv/model/runner
```

sara: stack traces show `cudaMemcpyAsync` failures followed by kernel resets. nodes report dmesg: `NVRM: GPU at 0000:64:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus` and intermittent PCIe errors.

kai: can we isolate whether it's hardware flakiness or a workload pattern? I can repro locally with a smaller repro if we throttle batch size.

eng-sre-oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 
- route traffic off gnode-07/08/09 (cordon+drain)
- enable single-GPU fallback model variant for affected customer buckets
- temporarily reduce batch_size to 1 for pipeline stages to avoid large prefetched KV state
- set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and capture `nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR` and core dumps
- collect containerd logs + dmesg and upload to /incidents/3659997777/artifacts

jonah: commands for drain: 
```
kubectl cordon gnode-07
kubectl drain gnode-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```
follow same for 08/09. Also increase restart backoff so we don't thrash.

infra-bot: cordon/drain issued for gnode-07 at 09:13:12Z, gnode-08 at 09:14:02Z. Scheduled gracePeriod 30s.

maria: snapshot of `nvidia-smi -q` from gnode-07: 
```
Fan Speed: 0 %
Temperature: 85 C
GPU Utilization: 95 %
ECC Errors: 0
Retired Pages: 0
```
Also see repeated `Xid 63` prior to `Xid 73` in the hour before.

sara: customers A and B (ids 1042, 2119) show increased request latency and errors. switching them to fallback now. rolling config update to routing: set `policy: prefer-single-gpu` for those customers.

maria: uploading tarball of dmesg+container logs to s3://redwood-incidents/3659997777/logs.tar.gz

eng-sre-oncall: investigation notes so far: 
- pattern consistent with a noisy GPU (thermal/PCIe) causing device resets -> NCCL communicator aborts -> hung collectives -> container OOM/restart due to KV cache corruption on pipeline stage
- not a model code regression; verts unaffected on other pools without those nodes

kai: quick mitigation idea: set `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` on affected nodes to avoid certain PCIe p2p paths, and force fallback to network-based collectives. Might reduce perf but improve reliability while we repro. Thoughts?

jonah: approve `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` for gnode-07/08/09 until we clear hardware. Apply as a node pool env override so it hits all server replicas.

eng-sre-oncall: applying env override now. also toggling `SERVING_BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS=512` -> 256 for affected pool.

infra-bot: env override applied to pool prod-serving-3 at 09:18:45Z. 12 pods restarted with new env.

maria: after changes, error rate dropped to ~2.1% within 4m. latency improved by ~120ms p95 for affected routes. still seeing occasional Xid 73 on gnode-09.

sara: while we stabilize, recommend scheduling immediate hardware swap for gnode-09 and replacement of PCIe riser on gnode-07 (vendor hotline already opened).

jonah: customer comms: draft for CX: "We're experiencing transient inference errors on a small subset of large-GPU instances; we've routed your traffic to a resilient configuration and are investigating hardware. You may see slightly increased latency while we run on fallback. We'll update in 1h or on resolution." Anyone object?

maria: good to send. add note that inference correctness isn't compromised (no model outputs lost), only availability/latency.

eng-sre-oncall: sending to CX now, marking incident P1 and creating follow-up ticket INF-7654 for hardware remediation + postmortem.

kai: for long-term: add node-level health probes for `nvidia-smi -q` thermal/PCIe counters, and a watcher to proactively drain nodes when error counts spike. Also evaluate making NCCL fallback policy global when Xid rate crosses threshold.

jonah: agree. add to postmortem actions.

eng-sre-oncall: handoff note for next shift (09:30Z): 
- incident active but stabilized; error rate down to 1.8%
- gnode-07/08 cordoned/drained, gnode-09 flagged for replacement (vendor ticket #VND-9921)
- mitigation flags: `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` applied to prod-serving-3, `SERVING_BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS=256` for affected pool
- artifacts: logs at s3://redwood-incidents/3659997777/logs.tar.gz, core dumps at s3://redwood-incidents/3659997777/cores/
- follow-ups: INF-7654 (hardware replacement), INF-7655 (probe/watchdog), PM-flag for perf regression when fallback is used

sara: adding final item: run a canary verification for the replaced nodes before returning them to pool; include a stress test for pipeline parallel with target batch sizes.

eng-sre-oncall: copying to #postmortems. handing off to @kai for overnight watch. Marking thread resolved for pager.

kai: got it. I'll keep an eye and will escalate if Xid spike returns. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
